thesis: Paul Black argues that while growth investing can be fun, the most rapidly growing companies can be massive destroyers of capital if not properly evaluated. He emphasizes that his early career was defined by learning from mistakes, particularly the realization that he needed to educate himself rather than relying on mentors to avoid capital destruction.
